macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rebounds as semiconductors offset Middle East anxiety
items.summary: U.S. stocks recovered, led by semiconductor strength, as investors balanced tech optimism against renewed concern over Iran and the wider Middle East conflict. MarketScreener also noted the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.60% and the S&P 500 gained 0.75%, while Brent crude fell 4.01%.

items.title: Risk appetite lifts global markets; dollar eases as Fed expectations shift
items.summary: Bloomberg Línea reported that European and Asian equities advanced while the dollar retreated as investors adjusted expectations for Federal Reserve policy. The report linked the move to a U.S. tech-led rally that pushed the S&P 500 up 0.8% and the Nasdaq 100 up 1.7%.

items.title: European stocks rise modestly as oil falls on Iran-related developments
items.summary: Finanzas.com said European indices rose moderately, supported by technology gains on Wall Street and a drop in oil prices amid Middle East negotiations. It also reported the IBEX 35 up 1.18% to 19,575 points, near historical highs.

items.title: Bank of Japan signals more rate hikes if inflation stays above target
items.summary: Bloomberg Línea reported that BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said the central bank may need additional rate increases if inflation risks persist above 2%, with timing dependent in part on the impact of the Iran conflict. The development adds to global central-bank focus even as markets price shifting policy paths.

items.title: ECB tightens policy and raises inflation outlook
items.summary: Finanzas.com reported that the European Central Bank raised rates for the first time since 2023, prioritizing inflation control over growth concerns. It also said the ECB lifted its 2026 inflation forecast to 3%.

items.title: Fed’s Waller calls for flexibility in forward guidance
items.summary: Europa Press reported that Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller defended forward guidance but urged greater flexibility in setting policy. The comments add to market scrutiny over the Fed’s next moves.

items.title: Intel jumps on strong market debut, highlighting semiconductor strength
items.summary: Bloomberg Línea said Intel shares surged as much as 12% in New York trading, reaching a record high. The move underscored investor enthusiasm for semiconductors and broader AI-linked hardware names.

items.title: Getty Images surges after OpenAI licensing deal
items.summary: Finanzas.com reported that Getty Images rose as much as 200% in premarket trading after announcing a strategic licensing agreement with OpenAI. The deal allows Getty images to be integrated into ChatGPT, sharply improving sentiment around the company.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs see $240M in outflows as market weakens
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $240 million in net outflows, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with $212 million exiting the fund. The move came alongside broader softness in crypto prices and risk appetite.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, and Solana all fall over 24 hours
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $61,913, down 2.2% in 24 hours, while Ether fell 2.3%, XRP dropped 3.9%, and Solana declined 5.2%. The pullback reflects a broad selloff across major digital assets.

items.title: SEC prepares major crypto regulatory overhaul
items.summary: The SEC is expected to release a major 'Regulation Crypto' agenda this month, signaling a potential shift in U.S. digital asset oversight. The same report says India is also weighing tighter crypto restrictions, including a possible blanket ban.

items.title: Galaxy Research lowers odds of Clarity Act passage
items.summary: Galaxy Research cut its estimate for the Clarity Act's 2026 passage to 30%, citing concerns about Senate voting dynamics. The update adds uncertainty around the U.S. crypto market structure bill.

items.title: Coinbase leadership shakeup hits legal, HR, and Base teams
items.summary: Coinbase reshuffled its top leadership as several senior heads stepped down, including leaders tied to legal, human resources, and Base. The changes come as the exchange faces an important regulatory period in the U.S.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $63K as risk sentiment improves
items.summary: Bitcoin moved back above $63,000 in a separate market update, helped by easing oil prices and improved risk appetite. The report also notes that broader crypto markets remain volatile.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission is requiring crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication, reflecting a stricter approach to cybersecurity controls. The change affects exchange operating standards in the jurisdiction.

items.title: XRP gains attention as Ripple-linked banking use expands
items.summary: XRP-related news highlighted SWIFT using Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments, supporting renewed interest in the asset. The report frames the development as a notable project and adoption story.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36M Nevada Bitcoin mining factory
items.summary: Bitdeer announced a new $36 million mining facility in Nevada, adding to industry investment in U.S.-based Bitcoin infrastructure. The project is part of ongoing mining expansion despite weaker market conditions.

items.title: LayerZero plans to retire support for 20 low-activity chains
items.summary: LayerZero said it will phase out support for 20 chains between July and September, requiring users to bridge assets before deadlines to avoid losses. The move is a significant ecosystem management change for the interoperability protocol.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT that can execute tasks across different applications and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools. Reuters said the release intensifies competition in workplace automation and business software.

items.title: OpenAI releases new real-time voice models
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models designed to listen and speak simultaneously in real time. Reuters said the models are part of OpenAI’s push into more natural voice interactions.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark AI model
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model along with an upgraded version, making it available for broader use through a public API preview. Reuters said the move puts Meta in closer competition with Anthropic and OpenAI on commercial AI access.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and positioning it for coding and agentic tasks. Reuters and other AI news outlets said the launch is part of a broader trend toward models optimized for autonomous workflows.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip production starting in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September as it works to expand its computing capacity. The memo reflects the industry-wide shift toward custom AI silicon to support rising inference and training demand.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move underscores continued governance and safety emphasis among frontier AI labs.

items.title: Mistral releases OCR 4 document-intelligence model
items.summary: Daily AI Briefing reported that Mistral launched OCR 4, a document-intelligence model supporting 170 languages with bounding boxes, block classification, and inline confidence scores in a self-hosted container. The release highlights continued competition in enterprise document AI.

items.title: Alibaba unveils Qwen Robot Suite for embodied AI
items.summary: AI Briefing reported that Alibaba introduced Qwen Robot Suite, including models for navigation, world modeling, and manipulation. The announcement points to growing competition in embodied AI and robotics-oriented foundation models.

items.title: NVIDIA introduces faster inference and science tools
items.summary: AI Briefing reported that NVIDIA introduced DFlash speculative decoding, claiming up to 15x faster Blackwell inference, alongside a BioNeMo Agent Toolkit for AI-driven science. The developments reinforce the trend toward optimizing AI infrastructure and scientific workflows.

items.title: Ollama raises $65 million to support local AI model deployment
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Ollama raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Venture. The company’s funding reflects strong investor interest in tools that let developers run open-weight models locally.
